pathogen.value: Infectious bursal disease virus (IBDV), a double-stranded RNA virus

value: spreads through contaminated food, water and physical contact
shed in feces and carried from house to house on contaminated equipment or clothing
birds huddled together with heads lowered

mortality.value: Around 20% with death within 3 to 4 days in clinical outbreaks
Morbidity often reaches 100% of the flock; mortality usually low but can range from 5% to over 60% depending on the virus strain and breed

diagnosis.value: Based on flock history, clinical signs and post-mortem exam, confirmed by lab detection of the virus
Gross and microscopic lesions in the bursa near the vent, plus molecular detection of the virus

value: vaccinating breeder flocks so chicks get protective antibodies from the hen
strict biosecurity limiting farm visits and contact with other flocks

treatment_overview.value: No specific treatment exists; management relies on vaccination and prevention since the virus survives a long time in housing and water

summary.value: Infectious bursal disease, also known as Gumboro disease, is a highly contagious viral infection that mainly strikes young chickens between about three and six weeks old, attacking the immune system by destroying cells in the bursa. There is no treatment, so prevention through vaccination of breeder flocks and strong biosecurity is the main defense, since surviving birds are left more vulnerable to other infections.
